summary: Completed public API and end-to-end SPA smoke testing for MJD Kupi. Core desktop demo flows pass; the backend remains only a generic status API and mobile layout has horizontal overflow.

critical.endpoint: POS, inventory, expenses, products, reports, tables APIs
critical.issue: No requested business APIs exist; backend exposes only /api/ and /api/status, so SPA data mutations are local-only and cannot sync with Supabase/backend.

ui_bugs.issue: document.documentElement.scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth at 390px, causing horizontal page overflow.

integration_issues.issue: All tested mutations use React state/localStorage; no backend or Supabase synchronization is wired.

action_items: Implement requested POS/ERP backend APIs and persistence or explicitly scope the product as frontend-only demo.
Investigate the overflowing mobile child and constrain layout at 390px.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js contains all modules and business state in one file; backend server.py is still starter scaffold and does not support the stated ERP integration.
Export CSV and QR/print actions are demo-only browser/UI behavior, not connected integrations.

success_rate.backend: 100% for available starter status API; 0% for requested ERP APIs
success_rate.frontend: 95% desktop flows; 90% overall due mobile overflow

seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_review_regression status record through the public starter API.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Desktop navigation, POS search/cart/payment/receipt, inventory restock, expense add, product add, report export, QR feedback, role switch all passed. Continue with backend business API coverage after implementation and retest mobile overflow.
rca of the issue: The missing backend integration is structural: server.py defines only the generated status-check router while App.js mutates local React state and localStorage directly. Mobile overflow was reproduced at 390x844 by comparing document scrollWidth and clientWidth; exact overflowing child was not isolated during this smoke pass.
